text: The canonical form of a workspace.json project path names `/` as the segment separator but does not say what a backslash is: a segment character or a non-canonical separator. The old loose rule treated `\` as a separator. Assumed: a path containing `\` is not canonical and makes workspace.json off the shape (on Windows it would name a different directory than on POSIX). Also not stated: a Windows drive prefix such as `C:/x` — it passes as a segment `C:` under the `/`-only rule.
assumption: ASSUMPTION:dev-6901 — a backslash is not a separator of the canonical form; a path carrying one is refused rather than read as a segment name, because on Windows it would name a different directory than on POSIX.
